title: Sri Lanka Chase 430 to Beat England Despite Brook's Record 202
excerpt: Harry Brook hit the fastest ODI double century in history, 202 off 116 balls in Rawalpindi, but Pavan Rathnayake's 130 led Sri Lanka to a two-wicket win with one ball left.
body:
• Harry Brook scored 202 off 116 balls, the first ODI double century by an England batter and the fastest in history, reaching 200 in 114 balls.
  • England posted 429 for 4 in Rawalpindi, their fourth-highest ODI total and the highest ODI total made in Pakistan.
  • Sri Lanka chased 430 for 8 in 49.5 overs to win by two wickets, the second-highest successful chase in ODI history.
  • Pavan Rathnayake made 130, Avishka Fernando and Dasun Shanaka both made 97, and Janith Liyanage hit an unbeaten 61 off 27 balls to finish the game.

Harry Brook made history in Rawalpindi on Thursday and still finished on the losing side. The England captain smashed 202 from 116 balls, with 21 fours and 10 sixes, to become the first England batter to score a double century in a one-day international, according to Reuters. Sri Lanka replied with 430 for 8 and won by two wickets with one ball to spare.

Brook reached 200 in 114 balls, three balls faster than the previous record of 117 set by India's Shubman Gill against the West Indies last month. He passed Ben Stokes' 182, the previous England ODI record, during an innings that started slowly — 13 runs from his first 24 balls — before he made a 75-ball century and added 156 runs with Will Jacks in the final 10 overs.

England pile up 429

England were put in to bat and built steadily through Tom Banton, who made 50 off 51 balls, and Joe Root, who scored 69 off 66 balls and became the first England batter to reach 8,000 ODI runs. Root and Brook shared 159 runs before Root fell, and Jacks then struck 66 not out off 30 balls, with eight fours and three sixes, as England closed on 429 for 4 in 50 overs.

https://x.com/SriLankaTweet/status/2113305256117645742

Brook was caught by Sahan Arachchige off Janith Liyanage from the final ball of the innings. At the break, England's total looked decisive. It was their fourth-highest score in ODIs and, as the BBC report carried in match coverage noted, the highest total made in a one-day international in Pakistan at that point.

"It was a nice innings but being on the losing side it has no value whatsoever in my eyes."

— Harry Brook, England captain

Sri Lanka refuse to fade

Sri Lanka slipped to 24 for 2 after Josh Tongue dismissed Kamindu Mendis and Kusal Mendis was run out without facing a ball. Pavan Rathnayake and Avishka Fernando rebuilt with a 166-run third-wicket stand. Fernando fell for 97, top-edging Jamie Overton, but Rathnayake went on to 130 off 106 balls, with 15 fours and three sixes.

Dasun Shanaka kept the chase moving with 97, hitting eight sixes and six fours, in a 133-run stand with Rathnayake off 79 balls. Sri Lanka still needed 109 from the final 10 overs and eight from the final over. Tongue bowled Dunith Wellalage and Eshan Malinga with successive balls, leaving six needed from two balls. Liyanage, who finished 61 not out off 27 balls, hit the penultimate delivery over long-off for six to seal the win, as reported by SuperSport and DAZN.

What the result means

The chase is second only to South Africa's 438 against Australia in Johannesburg in 2006 in ODI history. Sri Lanka captain Kusal Mendis said his side believed throughout: "Everyone believed we can do it. Every day we talk about showing the character in team meetings, and it's about showing we can get any score."

For England, the defeat was their second in two matches in the Pakistan tri-series, leaving them needing wins in their remaining games to reach the final in Lahore. Their attack, without Jofra Archer, who was rested, and Adil Rashid, who was left out, could not defend 429. Sam Curran conceded 103 runs in nine overs. Full match details are in the Reuters match report.

Brook's record will stand in the books — the 14th double hundred in men's ODIs and the fastest ever — but the night belonged to Sri Lanka's chase.
